items.title: Naive derived completion and derived completion agree exactly when the f-power torsion is bounded
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: With I = (f), the lemma compares the naive derived completion K' = R lim (K tensor^L_A A/f^nA) with the derived completion K^wedge = R lim (K tensor^L_A (A -> f^n -> A)) of the Koszul-complex statement, and asserts that the natural transformation K^wedge -> K' is an isomorphism for all K if and only if the f-power torsion of A is bounded (source lines 26810-26822). The forward implication is short: if the f-power torsion is bounded, the pro-objects {(f^n : A -> A)} and {A/f^nA} are isomorphic by the lifting statement, hence the functors are isomorphic by the equality of R lim on pro-equal pro-objects (proof lines 26825-26828). The converse is the substantial direction. From the exactness statement for tensor and R lim one gets that the condition is exactly that R lim (K tensor^L_A A[f^n]) vanishes for all K in D(A), the maps of the system (A[f^n]) being multiplication by f (proof lines 26829-26834). Taking K = A and K = bigoplus over N of A, the R lim of direct sums statement forces (A[f^n]) to be zero as a pro-object, that is f^{n-1}A[f^n] = 0 for some n, which is equivalent to A[f^{n-1}] = A[f^n], that is, bounded f-power torsion (proof lines 26835-26840). The non-routine content is the design of the converse: the two test complexes are chosen so that the vanishing of R lim on their tensor products detects the pro-triviality of the system of f-power torsion modules.
